name: Volume Converter
description: Convert volume between milliliters, liters, cubic meters, US cups/pints/quarts/gallons, imperial gallons, and cubic feet instantly.

faq.question: Why are there two kinds of gallon?
faq.answer: The US gallon (3.785411784 L) and the imperial (UK) gallon (4.54609 L) are genuinely different sizes — an imperial gallon is about 20% larger. Recipes, fuel economy figures, and container sizes all depend on which one applies, so both are listed separately rather than picking one as "the" gallon.

faq.question: Are the US cup/tablespoon/teaspoon here the cooking measurements or the exact legal US customary units?
faq.answer: The exact US customary definitions (used for the underlying math), which match standard US measuring cups/spoons closely enough for any practical recipe use — the tiny fractional differences from some countries' "metric cup" (250 mL exactly) or "metric tablespoon" (15 mL exactly) conventions are not the units used here.
